name: Lilac-Grey
lede: Lilac-Grey is a pale, warm-leaning light grey with only a whisper of violet, a name carried over from Ridgway's color nomenclature.

sections.title: A grey with a flower's hint
sections.body: Our library traces Lilac-Grey to Ridgway's Nomenclature of Colors of 1886, carried over to his plate LII of 1912 [1]. The ISCC-NBS system places it at light gray, only 1.9 units away on the CIEDE2000 scale [1]. At that distance the swatch is almost the standard grey, and the lilac is mostly in the name [1]. For the flower color itself, see [[lilac]].

sections.title: Lilac greys in painting
sections.body: The Pigment Compendium quotes Church (1901) recommending artificial Indian red, mixed with ultramarine, Prussian blue, indigo, or indigo and yellow ochre, for the lilac greys of stormy clouds in the English watercolor school [2]. The recipe shows how painters made such a grey: a small red-brown pulled against a blue [2]. St Clair's glossary uses the same idea for pearl, a very pale lilac-gray [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a color this close appears in 697 works, or 2.9 per cent, more than 83 per cent of the named colors [4]. It peaks in the 1900s, at 4.8 per cent of 1,674 paintings, twice the expected rate for the same museums [4]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so a match is not a pigment test [4].
